title: Latin and Greek roots
description: Common roots and prefixes that let you work out words you have never seen.

ideas.title: Greek roots for words and knowing
ideas.summary: Greek gave English its roots for word, writing, sound, time and study.
links: Greek roots for life and mind

items.q: What does the Greek root "graph" mean, as in "biography" and "telegraph"?
What does the ending "-logy" mean, as in "geology" and "theology"?
items.a: The study of (from Greek logos, word or reason)

items.q: The Greek roots "tele" and "phon" make the word "telephone". What does each mean?
items.a: Tele means far; phon means sound

items.q: What does the Greek root "chron" mean, as in "chronic" and "synchronize"?
From its Greek roots, what does the word "philosophy" literally mean?
items.a: Love of wisdom (philo, loving + sophia, wisdom)

ideas.title: Greek roots for life and mind
ideas.summary: A few Greek roots name human beings, the mind and feeling, and they combine freely with one another.
links: Greek roots for words and knowing
Prefixes of good, bad and not

items.q: What does the Greek root "anthrop" mean, as in "anthropology" and "philanthropy"?
What does the Greek root "path" mean, as in "sympathy" and "pathology"?
Which Greek root, meaning mind or soul, begins the words "psychology" and "psychiatry"?
From its Greek roots, what does the word "misanthrope" literally mean?
items.a: A hater of humankind (misein, to hate + anthropos, human being)

ideas.title: Latin roots for common actions
ideas.summary: Latin verbs for say, look, carry, believe and lead sit inside hundreds of English words.

items.q: What does the Latin root "dict" mean, as in "predict" and "dictate"?
What does the Latin root "spec" or "spect" mean, as in "inspect" and "spectator"?
Which Latin root, meaning "to carry", is shared by "transport", "portable" and "import"?
What does the Latin root "cred" mean, as in "credible" and "creed"?
What does the Latin root "duc" or "duct" mean, as in "conduct" and "aqueduct"?

ideas.title: Prefixes of place and direction
ideas.summary: Prefixes such as sub-, super-, inter- and circum- say where something is or which way it goes.
links: Prefixes of good, bad and not

items.q: What is the difference between the prefixes "inter-" and "intra-"?
items.a: Inter- means between; intra- means within

items.q: What do the Greek prefixes "hyper-" and "hypo-" mean?
items.a: Hyper- means over or above; hypo- means under or below

items.q: What do the Latin prefixes "sub-" and "super-" mean?
items.a: Sub- means under; super- means above or over

items.q: What is the difference between the prefixes "ante-" and "anti-"?
items.a: Ante- means before; anti- means against

items.q: From its Latin parts, what does the word "circumspect" literally mean?

ideas.title: Prefixes of good, bad and not
ideas.summary: Bene- and eu- mark the good, mal- and dys- the bad, and a- or an- the absent.
links: Greek roots for life and mind
